entries.body_en: Its siblings mix pigment by hand. This one asks the physics what colour comes back and prints that answer.
entries._audit_body_en: MINERALIA-016 shipped 2026-08-25 as the deck's first physics-sourced card. Colour: Michel-Levy interference, I(l)=sin^2(2t)*sin^2(pi*G/l) integrated against the CIE 1931 2-degree observer using the Wyman/Sloan/Shirley (JCGT 2(2), 2013) multi-lobe piecewise-Gaussian fit, precomputed to a 7000-entry linear-light LUT at 5nm sampling (measured identical to 1nm within 1/255). Validated against an independent implementation of the Sorensen 2013 (EJM 25(1) 5-10) pipeline on 19 checkpoints: worst channel delta 11/255, and it passes the discriminating case where the CALCULATED chart returns turquoise at 730nm while the PRINTED chart shows saturated green. Ground truth holds unprompted at the standard 30um section: quartz lands on first-order white, calcite on high-order pearl. Fabric: a Johnson-Mehl growth, not a Voronoi partition. Fronts nucleate in time, advance at a rate through a convex crystal-habit (Wulff) metric, and are blocked by whatever crystallised first, so porphyritic and interstitial textures emerge from one rule rather than being drawn. Voronoi is the simultaneous-nucleation isotropic-growth case, which no rock obeys. Interior: polysynthetic and Carlsbad twinning, oscillatory zoning on polygon insets with resorption truncations, band-limited exsolution synthesised as 14 plane waves at one |k| (spinodal decomposition has energy at ONE scale where fbm has it at all), undulose strain, spherulites, and oikocryst families that share a hidden orientation so disconnected grains blink to black in unison. Section: thickness field, Becke-line relief scaled by |n_grain - n_balsam|, fractures, mounting-medium dust. Every one of those moves RETARDATION or ORIENTATION, never brightness, so a thin place is a different colour rather than a darker one. Four lights: crossed polars, plane light with spectrally-correct pleochroism, the sensitive tint plate as a fixed retardation offset, and a conoscopic interference figure (uniaxial cross locked to the polars with isochromes as LUT[k*r^2]; biaxial isogyres as the zero set of sin(a1+a2-2t) with Cassinian isochromes). Kill-test asserts the physics first: 18/18, run 8 consecutive times. Three defects found and fixed at the layer rather than the surface: a two-face Wulff metric is an infinite slab and every mica grew clear across the frame; nucleation time anchored to a constant instead of the typical grain radius let one crystal own the frame; separable sin(x)*cos(y) noise put an axis-aligned cross-hatch on every large grain.
